title: Illinois's 4th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Illinois's 4th Congressional District is an open-seat race following the retirement of incumbent Democrat Jesús 'Chuy' García, who decided not to seek a fifth term. The district, which covers parts of Chicago's Southwest Side and western suburbs including Cicero, Berwyn, and portions of DuPage County, is overwhelmingly Democratic (Cook Political Report rating: Solid D). The race has been marked by controversy after Rep. García bowed out on the last day for candidate filing, clearing a path for his chief of staff, Patty Garcia (no relation), to become the sole Democratic candidate on the primary ballot — a move that prompted several prominent Democrats to launch independent campaigns. The general election features Democratic nominee Patty Garcia, Republican nominee Lupe Castillo, and multiple independent challengers, including Chicago Alderman Byron Sigcho-Lopez and former Obama campaign organizer Mayra Macias.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of June 2026.

candidates.name: Patty Garcia
candidates.summary: Patty Garcia is the Democratic nominee for Illinois's 4th Congressional District and the outgoing congressman's handpicked successor. She has served as chief of staff and district director for Rep. Jesús 'Chuy' García since 2019, managing the district office and overseeing constituent services. She holds a PhD in Education Policy from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and has over 15 years of experience working with immigrant and working-class families. Her campaign focuses on immigration reform, cost-of-living relief, health care access, and continuing the progressive agenda of the retiring congressman.

candidates.name: Lupe Castillo
candidates.summary: Lupe Castillo is the Republican nominee for Illinois's 4th Congressional District, having advanced unopposed from the March 17 primary. She is a former 22nd Ward Republican Committeewoman on Chicago's Southwest Side and previously ran for this seat in 2024, losing to incumbent Jesús 'Chuy' García by a wide margin. Castillo describes herself as a conservative who supports strengthening border security, protecting Second Amendment rights, and reducing federal spending. Her campaign emphasizes representing all communities within the district, including suburban DuPage County.

candidates.name: Byron Sigcho-Lopez
candidates.summary: Byron Sigcho-Lopez is an independent candidate for Illinois's 4th Congressional District and has served as Chicago's 25th Ward Alderman since 2019. An immigrant from Ecuador and a former teacher, he is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America and a close ally of Mayor Brandon Johnson. He announced his independent bid after criticizing the process that made Patty Garcia the sole Democratic nominee, calling it an 'anti-democratic back room deal.' His platform includes abolishing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, supporting Medicare for All, and increasing taxes on large corporations and the ultra-wealthy.

candidates.name: Mayra Macias
candidates.summary: Mayra Macias is an independent candidate for Illinois's 4th Congressional District and a lifelong Democrat who previously served as a field organizer for President Barack Obama's 2012 re-election campaign. A former teacher and Back of the Yards native, she also served as executive director of the Latino Victory Fund and Building Back Together. She launched her independent bid in December 2025, criticizing Rep. García's last-minute retirement and the process that cleared the path for his chief of staff. Macias has been endorsed by Planned Parenthood Action Fund and End Citizens United, and her platform focuses on making life more affordable, protecting immigrant communities, and defending democracy.

candidates.name: Chris Getty
candidates.summary: Chris Getty is an independent candidate for Illinois's 4th Congressional District and has served as Mayor of Lyons, Illinois, since 2009, when he was elected at age 26. He filed his independent nominating petitions on May 18, 2026, collecting thousands of signatures. Getty has criticized outgoing Rep. García for what he called 'machine politics' and a lack of tangible results for the district. He argues that being from the suburbs is an asset, as a majority of the district's general election voters live in suburban areas. His campaign priorities include comprehensive immigration reform.
